status: Architecture review and scratch storage experiments; not a production migration or statewide acceptance result
reason: User challenged premature publication of a tiny standalone slice and directed work toward the data model and solver foundation.
confirmedProduct: Generate trail hikes. Roads and sidewalks may reach trails or connect trails. Entirely urban sidewalk walks are outside the intended experience.
Map and named areas select starting places; storage divisions must not clip routes.
Local first, automatic prepared-data acquisition, browser reconnect while the server runs; hosting remains deferred.
Long searches are acceptable. Preserve useful coverage and disclose unfinished exploration.

recommendedDirection.model: One versioned physical network, partitioned for delivery and selective reading. Independently clipped regional graphs are not composable by current IDs.
recommendedDirection.storage: Prefer immutable geographic files, with starts, compact topology, and geometry separate. Physical encoding and the source builder remain provisional until source, seam, coverage and whole-app checks pass.
recommendedDirection.identity: Junctions and physical trail sections share identity across every file in one snapshot. No requirement for permanent compiled identities across releases. Retain source lineage for audit.
recommendedDirection.routeFacts: Preserve trail/road/sidewalk classification, physical section identity, direction-specific foot permission and gain, and real junction connectivity. Handle passage restrictions separately from trail existence.
recommendedDirection.starts: Keep the network attachment, naming, walking permission and evidence of trailhead/parking/road contact distinct. A road contact is not a parking guarantee.
recommendedDirection.coverage: Pin source and processing versions. Distinguish covered empty cells, missing files and unprepared geography. A finished traversal is not evidence of complete geography.
recommendedDirection.query: Select starts, then read a conservative geographic superset for their maximum closed-route length. Keep whole intersecting sections and endpoints. The current prototype uses a D/2 + 1m geographic enclosure, relying on the production distance metric invariant.
recommendedDirection.geometry: Retain measured elevation/drawing profiles separately and read them on route inspection; never eagerly load all geometry for every search.
recommendedDirection.serving: Static prepared files can be acquired and cached by a small local server. The CPU worker searches a compact working network. No hosted database or remote trail query is required for the confirmed local experience.

verifiedCurrentProblems: Current eager graph plus geometry loading peaks at 616284160 bytes on the broad Cascades artifact before any solver runs.
Current corridor IDs depend on local compaction anchors and footprint clipping: 79 original North Bend corridor IDs are absent from the broader build.
Removing one redundant access point replaced two corridor IDs with one without changing underlying source segments.
Generated clipped frontier IDs omit cut coordinates and are unsafe as shared identities across independently prepared regions.
The compiled runtime representation discards the source distinction between hiking paths and sidewalks/roads.
The broader compiler currently holds large source, sampled-profile and output structures simultaneously; its measured 2358902784-byte peak is not a statewide feasibility result.

sourceInventory.scope: Frozen Washington OSM extract, including complete source ways outside its nominal boundary. These are source counts, not routing graph counts or a statewide build.

fullCurrentEagerLoader.caveat: Fresh process; OS file cache not controlled. Eager-loading only, no solver or HTTP/browser.

limitations: Fresh Node processes, uncontrolled OS filesystem cache. Individual observations, not statistical performance conclusions.
Partial readers materialize compact topology and local node indices; they do not build adjacency, run search or include browser/server memory.
The eager-loader baseline includes all geometry; partial readers intentionally do not. This is an architecture comparison, not equal-payload timing.
Both prototype importers first materialize the existing whole snapshot; neither proves bounded preparation at statewide scale.
File chunking does not make very broad or long exhaustive searches cheap.
Geographic files require integrity checks, coherent snapshots, explicit missing coverage and bounded cache behavior before production use.
Scratch code and full reports remain local; this record does not claim a maintained or portable benchmark harness.

alternatives.assessment: Valid local store with spatial indexes and per-section geometry reads. Rejected as the current delivery preference because partial acquisition would need an additional scheme; not rejected for scale limits.
Reject as the logical data model: regional overlap and clipping change identity and can sever cross-region hikes.
Retain only as the current slice baseline; eager loading does not meet the intended scale model.

Serious source-builder alternative. Official graph access and elevation profiles exist. Lossless base-network export, explicit access evidence, barrier semantics and cumulative elevation measurements require a small proof before choosing it or continuing custom preparation.
No confirmed local-product need justifies a mandatory service.

nextEvidenceRequired: A real hike crossing storage divisions retains identical connectivity, measurements and physical repetition; missing pieces cannot look like no route.
Source preparation preserves agreed hiking versus connector semantics and explicit restrictions, with independently checked access points and routes.
Measure statewide preparation and installed data rather than extrapolating the tiny slice. Stream or batch expensive source/elevation processing; expose unavailable coverage.
Run the frozen real-query acceptance cases through the actual worker/server with partial loading, including long hikes, cancellation, memory and honest completion.
